title: openai-compat: improve tool schema mapping, tool_choice semantics, and tool message formatting
author: Alex Park
description:
Motivation: The OpenAI compatibility layer has historically exposed tool/function calling but had subtle mismatches vs the OpenAI semantics around tool schema mapping, the tool_choice contract, and streaming tool message formatting. These mismatches caused: (1) client-facing schema/type inconsistencies when mapping OpenAI 'parameters' -> Redwood tool parameter types, (2) ambiguity in how 'tool_choice' is represented in streaming and final responses (index vs name vs id), and (3) corrupted/partial JSON arguments streamed for large tool calls which broke downstream tool runners.

What this PR does (single-string description): Implements deterministic mapping from OpenAI-style tool schemas (JSON Schema-like 'parameters' with types/properties/required) to Redwood tool parameter definitions; normalizes the tool_choice payload so that streaming events include both stable 'tool_id' (internal id) and 'tool_name' (user-facing name) plus a 'choice_index' for backward compatibility; fixes streaming tooling framing so partial argument chunks accumulate into valid JSON objects on the server side and are emitted to tool runners only after successful reassembly/validation; adds a compatibility layer that accepts legacy tool_choice shapes (string name or integer index) and translates them to the canonical structure; updates the OpenAI-compat docs and examples to show canonical tool_choice and mapping examples; adds unit and integration tests (including end-to-end streaming tests with large JSON arguments).

Implementation notes: - openai_compat/mapper.py: new mapping utilities to convert OpenAI 'parameters' -> redwood tool param schema (type coercions, default handling, required flags). - openai_compat/streaming.py: rework of streaming parser to buffer partial function_call/arguments and to emit a single 'tool_invoke' event only after JSON reassembly and schema validation. - openai_compat/choice_normalizer.py: canonicalizer that surfaces {tool_id, tool_name, choice_index} and accepts legacy forms. - docs/openai-compat.md: updated examples and migration notes. - tests/: added unit tests for mapping edge cases and integration test that simulates chunked streaming from an LLM.

Compatibility and rollout: The change is backward compatible: we accept legacy shapes and continue to emit the previous simple name-only shape under a deprecated flag for 1 minor release; with default behavior now returning the canonical shape. There are no breaking changes for existing customers, but SDKs should prefer the canonical fields when available.

Testing and validation: Extensive unit tests for schema mapping (type coercion: integer/number/string/boolean/array/object), streaming reassembly tests for large arguments (>64KB), integration test against the tool runner to ensure tools receive validated JSON. CI: all checks passing after two reruns (flaky e2e fixed by increased timeouts).

Follow-ups: - ENG-7290: expose mapping diagnostics in the console (reason for coercion/validation failures). - ENG-7312: add automated migration guide & deprecation warnings in client SDKs.

Checklist: - [x] Schema mapping utilities implemented - [x] tool_choice canonicalization implemented - [x] Streaming reassembly fixes implemented - [x] Unit + integration tests added - [x] Docs updated

review_comments: Maria Chen: Nice work — the mapper code is clean. Two nits: 1) add explicit handling for 'nullable' top-level props, 2) add an example for array-of-objects coercion.
Alex Park: Addressed both nits in latest commit; added nullable test and example in docs.
Daniel Kwan: Streaming reassembly looks good. One concern: buffering large args may increase memory pressure on busy workers — can we cap buffer size and fall back to tempfile?
Alex Park: Added a configurable buffer cap with tempfile fallback; default remains in-memory for small payloads. Added integration test for fallback path.
Priya Shah: Tests look thorough, and docs are clear. Approving.
CI Bot: e2e tests failed on first run (timeout). Reran with increased timeout, all checks passed.
release_notes: openai-compat: canonical tool_choice shape ({tool_id, tool_name, choice_index}) and improved mapping from OpenAI tool schemas to Redwood tool parameter types. Streaming tool arguments are now reassembled and validated before invocation, fixing issues with partial/fragmented JSON arguments. Backward-compatible and accepted legacy shapes for one release.
